text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, it is crucial to determine if this swelling could be a metastasis, so does the mass feel hard and fixed, or is it soft and mobile? speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal and the mass is located on the nape of the neck, this presentation is highly suggestive of a benign cystic lesion rather than a malignancy. Could you tell me if the swelling has ever drained any thick, foul-smelling material, and does it tend to enlarge or become more noticeable when you exercise?

text: The ultrasound confirms a well-circumscribed cystic lesion, which aligns with the history of a painless, progressively enlarging mass on the nape of the neck.
